svg.font-family: 'Geist Mono', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

metadata.orrery:spec: # yaml-language-server: $schema=../references/diagram.schema.json title: AI coding agent on the Model Context Protocol subtitle: The MCP host runs one MCP client per MCP server, over stdio locally and Streamable HTTP with OAuth remotely; Claude picks each tool and gets its result back direction: down legend: solid: Request dashed: MCP over stdio dotted: Telemetry groups: # Only the host is a group; local versus remote is in each server's note, as in the MCP architecture overview. host: { type: zone, label: MCP host (AI application) } nodes: dev: { icon: generic:user, label: Developer, note: IDE or terminal } agent: { icon: tabler:ai-agent, label: Agent loop, note: Tool registry, in: host } # The architecture docs: "The MCP host accomplishes this by creating one MCP client for each MCP server." client-fs: { icon: tabler:plug-connected, label: MCP client 1, in: host } client-gh: { icon: tabler:plug-connected, label: MCP client 2, in: host } client-db: { icon: tabler:plug-connected, label: MCP client 3, in: host } claude: { icon: logos:claude-icon, label: Claude, note: Anthropic API or Amazon Bedrock } fs: { icon: logos:model-context-protocol-icon, label: Filesystem server, note: Local subprocess } files: { icon: generic:files, label: Project files } gh: { icon: logos:model-context-protocol-icon, label: GitHub MCP server, note: "Remote, GitHub-hosted" } # The remote server is the OAuth resource server; GitHub's authorization server issues the token. oauth: { icon: generic:auth, label: GitHub OAuth, note: Authorization server } ghapi: { icon: logos:github-icon, label: GitHub, note: "Repos, issues, PRs" } pg: { icon: logos:model-context-protocol-icon, label: Postgres MCP server, note: "Remote, team-hosted" } db: { icon: logos:postgresql, label: PostgreSQL } otel: { icon: logos:opentelemetry-icon, label: OTel Collector } grafana: { icon: logos:grafana, label: Grafana Cloud, note: Traces and dashboards } edges: # One tool call against the GitHub server, in order. - dev -> agent: { label: prompt } # Written in layout order with the arrow flipped, so Claude sits beside the developer above the host. - { from: claude, to: agent, arrow: start, label: messages + tools } - agent -> client-gh: { label: tools/call } # Every HTTP request to the MCP endpoint carries the access token in an Authorization: Bearer header. - client-gh -> gh: { label: "Streamable HTTP, Bearer token" } - gh -> ghapi: { label: REST API } - client-gh -> oauth: OAuth 2.1 + PKCE - agent -> client-fs, client-db # stdio: the client launches the server as a subprocess; credentials come from the environment, not OAuth. - client-fs --> fs: stdio - fs -> files: read and write - client-db -> pg: Streamable HTTP - pg -> db: SQL - agent ..> otel: OTLP traces - otel ..> grafana

svg.title: AI coding agent on the Model Context Protocol
svg.desc: AI coding agent on the Model Context Protocol. 15 components in 1 groups. Connections: Developer to Agent loop (prompt); Claude to Agent loop (messages + tools); Agent loop to MCP client 2 (tools/call); MCP client 2 to GitHub MCP server (Streamable HTTP, Bearer token); GitHub MCP server to GitHub (REST API); MCP client 2 to GitHub OAuth (OAuth 2.1 + PKCE); Agent loop to MCP client 1; Agent loop to MCP client 3; MCP client 1 to Filesystem server (stdio); Filesystem server to Project files (read and write); MCP client 3 to Postgres MCP server (Streamable HTTP); Postgres MCP server to PostgreSQL (SQL); Agent loop to OTel Collector (OTLP traces); OTel Collector to Grafana Cloud.

text.tspan: AI CODING AGENT ON THE MODEL CONTEXT PROTOCOL
The MCP host runs one MCP client per MCP server, over stdio locally and Streamable HTTP with OAuth remotely; Claude
picks each tool and gets its result back
